sub_graphs.title: EIP-6051: Private Key Encapsulation Protocol Lifecycle
sub_graphs.description: Models the full lifecycle of private key encapsulation from key generation through decryption

nodes.label: Protocol Idle
nodes.description: No active key encapsulation session in progress

nodes.label: Generate Recipient Ephemeral Keys (R1)
nodes.description: Recipient generates random ephemeral key pair (r, R) using CSRNG

nodes.label: Recipient Ephemeral Keys Ready
nodes.description: Recipient has generated ephemeral key pair, optionally with signature

nodes.label: Transmit Recipient Public Key
nodes.description: Recipient's public key R is transmitted to sender

nodes.label: Sender Has Recipient Public Key
nodes.description: Sender has received recipient's ephemeral public key

nodes.label: Encapsulate Private Key (R2)
nodes.description: Sender encrypts private key using ECIES with recipient's public key

nodes.label: Private Key Encapsulated
nodes.description: Private key has been encrypted and is ready for transport

nodes.label: Transport Encrypted Key
nodes.description: Encrypted key (S || cipher) is transmitted to recipient

nodes.label: Recipient Has Encrypted Key
nodes.description: Recipient has received the encapsulated key data

nodes.label: Intake Private Key (R3)
nodes.description: Recipient decrypts the private key using stored ephemeral private key

nodes.label: Private Key Recovered
nodes.description: Recipient has successfully decrypted and recovered the private key

nodes.label: Securely Destroy Ephemeral Keys
nodes.description: Both sender and recipient destroy ephemeral keys to ensure PFS

nodes.label: Protocol Complete with PFS
nodes.description: Key transfer complete, ephemeral keys destroyed, perfect forward secrecy achieved

edges.label: Sender provides private key to encapsulate

external_entities.name: Sender Application
external_entities.description: Application holding the private key to be encapsulated and transferred

external_entities.name: Recipient Application
external_entities.description: Application that will receive and store the private key

sub_graphs.title: EIP-6051: ECIES Cryptographic Operations
sub_graphs.description: Models the detailed cryptographic operations during key encapsulation

nodes.label: Encapsulation Inputs Ready
nodes.description: Sender has private key to encapsulate and recipient's public key R

nodes.label: Generate Sender Ephemeral Key Pair
nodes.description: Generate random ephemeral key pair (s, S) for ECDH

nodes.label: Sender Ephemeral Keys Ready
nodes.description: Sender has generated ephemeral key pair (s, S)

nodes.label: Compute ECDH Shared Secret
nodes.description: Compute shared secret ss = ECDH(s, R) using sender's private and recipient's public

nodes.label: Shared Secret Computed
nodes.description: ECDH shared secret has been computed

nodes.label: Derive Symmetric Key and IV via HKDF
nodes.description: Use HKDF to derive symmetric key (skey) and initialization vector (IV) from shared secret

nodes.label: Symmetric Encryption Parameters Ready
nodes.description: Symmetric key and IV derived for AES-GCM encryption

nodes.label: Encrypt Private Key with AES-GCM
nodes.description: Encrypt the private key using derived symmetric key and IV

nodes.label: Ciphertext Ready
nodes.description: Private key has been encrypted into ciphertext

nodes.label: Concatenate S and Cipher
nodes.description: Combine sender's public key S with ciphertext for transport

nodes.label: Encapsulation Output Ready
nodes.description: Final output (S || cipher) ready for transmission

sub_graphs.title: EIP-6051: Signature and Trust Chain Validation
sub_graphs.description: Models the validation of signatures and trust chains during key encapsulation

nodes.label: Recipient Public Key Received
nodes.description: Sender has received recipient's public key with optional signature

nodes.label: Check if Signature Present
nodes.description: Determine if signerPubKey is provided for verification

nodes.label: No Signature Provided
nodes.description: Public key provided without signature, trust is implicit

nodes.label: Signature Provided
nodes.description: Public key includes signature from signerPubKey

nodes.label: Verify Signature on Public Key
nodes.description: Verify that R is correctly signed by signerPubKey using ECDSA/Ed25519

nodes.label: Signature Valid
nodes.description: Signature verification passed

nodes.label: Signature Invalid
nodes.description: Signature verification failed

nodes.label: Check Trust Chain (Optional)
nodes.description: If trustedPubKey provided, verify signerPubKey is signed by trustedPubKey

nodes.label: Trust Chain Valid
nodes.description: Full trust chain from trustedPubKey to R verified

nodes.label: Validation Complete
nodes.description: All validation checks passed, ready to proceed

nodes.label: Validation Failed
nodes.description: Validation failed, abort encapsulation

external_entities.name: Key Provider
external_entities.description: Entity providing the recipient's public key with optional signature

sub_graphs.title: EIP-6051: Security Boundaries and Key Protection
sub_graphs.description: Models the security boundaries and key protection mechanisms in the protocol

nodes.label: Private Key in Sender Memory
nodes.description: Private key exists in sender application memory before encapsulation

nodes.label: Verify Sender Verification Capability
nodes.description: Ensure sender can perform signature verification even with limited computing power

nodes.label: Sender Verification Capable
nodes.description: Sender has capability to verify signatures

nodes.label: Generate Keys with CSRNG
nodes.description: All ephemeral keys generated using cryptographically secure random number generator

nodes.label: Ephemeral Keys Securely Generated
nodes.description: Ephemeral keys have sufficient entropy from CSRNG

nodes.label: Encrypt Key for Untrusted Transport
nodes.description: Encrypt private key so it can traverse untrusted channels safely

nodes.label: Key Protected During Transport
nodes.description: Private key is encrypted and safe to transmit over untrusted channels

nodes.label: Securely Destroy Ephemeral Keys
nodes.description: Overwrite and destroy ephemeral key material after protocol completion

nodes.label: Perfect Forward Secrecy Achieved
nodes.description: Ephemeral keys destroyed, past ciphertexts cannot be decrypted

nodes.label: Private Key Securely at Recipient
nodes.description: Private key now exists only at recipient, original location cleared

external_entities.name: Original Key Holder
external_entities.description: Entity that currently holds the private key to be transferred

external_entities.name: Untrusted Transport Channel
external_entities.description: Network or channel over which encrypted key data is transmitted

ambiguities.text: The specification does not define what 'securely destroyed' means in practice for ephemeral keys
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume secure destruction means overwriting key memory with random data or zeros before deallocation, and ensuring no copies exist in swap or cache.

ambiguities.text: Sender application is described as potentially having 'very limited computing power' but must still perform signature verification
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume even resource-constrained devices can perform ECDSA/Ed25519 verification, which is computationally cheaper than signing.

ambiguities.text: The salt parameter is 'optional but recommended as 12-16 bytes' but no guidance on when it should be omitted
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume salt should always be used when available; omission is only for backward compatibility with systems that cannot provide it.

ambiguities.text: No specification for handling version negotiation when sender and recipient support different cryptographic versions
ambiguities.resolution_strategy: Assume secp256k1-AES-128-GCM is the mandatory baseline and all implementations must support it as a fallback.

implicit_assumptions.description: Both sender and recipient have access to cryptographically secure random number generators (CSRNG)
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Weak randomness in ephemeral key generation would allow attackers to predict keys and decrypt the transferred private key.

implicit_assumptions.description: Attackers cannot compromise both the sender and recipient applications simultaneously
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: If both endpoints are compromised, the private key can be intercepted regardless of encryption.

implicit_assumptions.description: The trustedPubKey (e.g., hardware wallet vendor) is trustworthy and its private key is not compromised
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Compromised trust anchor could sign malicious recipient public keys, enabling man-in-the-middle attacks.

implicit_assumptions.description: Quantum computers capable of breaking ECDH/ECDSA are not available to attackers
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: As noted in the spec, quantum computers would break the underlying cryptography, making the protocol insecure.

implicit_assumptions.description: Applications correctly implement ephemeral key destruction after protocol completion
implicit_assumptions.impact_if_false: Retained ephemeral keys would allow decryption of recorded ciphertexts, breaking perfect forward secrecy.
